title: Divorce in Bangladesh for Expats: Is Your UK, USA or UAE Divorce Valid?
metaTitle: Is a Foreign Divorce Valid in Bangladesh? Expat Guide
metaDescription: Living abroad and married in Bangladesh? Learn when a UK, US, UAE or Canadian divorce is recognised in Bangladesh, how talaq works under the MFLO 1961, and what to do about dower and custody.
heroIntro: Many expats marry in Bangladesh, move abroad and later divorce in the UK, USA, Canada or the Gulf. Then they discover that the divorce paper from the foreign court or registry is not automatically accepted in Bangladesh, which affects remarriage, inheritance, immigration sponsorship and dower rights. This guide is written by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, for Bangladeshis living in the UK, USA, UAE, Canada and elsewhere. For case-specific help you can call the chamber on 01712655546 or WhatsApp the same number.

quickAnswer.heading: Divorce for Expats: Key Points
points: For Muslims, talaq is governed by Section 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961: written notice to the Chairman and to the wife, and divorce takes effect after 90 days unless revoked.
A foreign divorce decree is not automatically valid in Bangladesh; recognition depends on whether the foreign court had jurisdiction and followed the law (Section 13, Code of Civil Procedure).
If you married in Bangladesh, the safest approach is to also complete the Bangladeshi legal formalities.
Hindu marriages and Christian marriages follow different laws (Hindu customary law and the Divorce Act 1869 for Christians).
Dower (denmohor), maintenance and child custody must be addressed whatever the divorce route.

toc: Foreign Court Divorce: When Is It Recognised?
Documents Needed and Steps for Expats

sections.content:
A divorce is a legal status. If a marriage was registered in Bangladesh and one or both spouses are Bangladeshi, the Bangladeshi system may still treat the marriage as continuing unless the divorce complies with Bangladesh law or is recognised under the rules on foreign judgments. If you remarry without clarity, you can face questions of bigamy, legitimacy of children and inheritance.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

Under Section 7 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, a Muslim husband who wants to divorce by talaq must:

  1. Pronounce talaq and give written notice to the Chairman (of the Union Parishad or City Corporation).
  2. Send a copy of the notice to the wife.
  3. Wait 90 days. The talaq takes effect after this period unless it has been revoked, or the wife is pregnant, in which case it takes effect after delivery.

An expat husband can send the notice by post or through an advocate and attorney. The Chairman then forms an Arbitration Council to try reconciliation. After 90 days, the divorce certificate (talaqnama) is issued.

A Muslim wife can obtain divorce in several ways:

  • Delegated talaq (Talaq-e-Tafweez): if the marriage contract (Kabinnama) gave her the power to divorce.
  • Khula: divorce by mutual consent, normally with the wife giving up her dower.
  • Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act 1939: suit in the Family Court on grounds such as desertion, cruelty, failure to maintain, or the husband's imprisonment.

Even if she lives abroad, she can file in the Family Court through her advocate or by Power of Attorney, though personal appearance may be needed for some stages.

sections.h2: Foreign Court Divorce: When Is It Recognised?
sections.content:
Bangladesh follows the principle in Section 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908: a foreign judgment is conclusive unless it was given by a court without jurisdiction, not on the merits, contrary to international or Bangladesh law, obtained by fraud, or opposes natural justice.

In practice, a divorce decree issued by a competent UK, US or Canadian court after a fair process, where both spouses took part, is more likely to be respected. A quick divorce obtained without notice to the Bangladeshi spouse, or a "paper talaq" from an overseas mosque only, is far more vulnerable to challenge.

To reduce risk, many Bangladeshi advocates recommend that the husband also serves the MFLO notice on the Chairman, or that the couple jointly file for registration of the divorce in Bangladesh.

Hindu marriages: there is no general codified divorce statute for Hindus in Bangladesh. Courts rely on custom and personal law, and a foreign divorce is generally scrutinised under Section 13 CPC.

Christian marriages: governed by the Divorce Act 1869 and the Christian Marriage Act 1872. A divorce is granted by the District Court on the specified grounds.

If you are in a mixed-faith marriage under the Special Marriage Act 1872, get tailored advice because rules differ.

• Dower (denmohor): the unpaid dower is a debt; the wife can claim it whether the divorce is local or foreign.
  • Maintenance: during the marriage and the iddat period, and for children until they are independent; the Family Courts Ordinance 1985 governs claims.
  • Custody and guardianship: decided by the Family Court under the Guardians and Wards Act 1890, with the welfare of the child as the controlling factor. Mothers generally keep young children (boys until about 7 and girls until puberty), but the courts look at the child's best interests.

Where a child lives abroad, enforcement across countries is difficult. Seek advice early to avoid parental abduction issues.

sections.h2: Documents Needed and Steps for Expats
sections.content:
1. Marriage certificate (Kabinnama) and NID/passport of both spouses.
  2. Foreign divorce decree or certificate (apostille/attested as required, with certified translation if not in English or Bangla).
  3. Proof of dower payment or claim, and any agreement on children.
  4. Power of Attorney to your Bangladesh advocate, notarised and attested at the Bangladesh Mission.
  5. Written notice under Section 7 MFLO, sent to the Chairman and the spouse.
  6. Obtain the divorce certificate and, if needed, register it with the local Nikah/Marriage Registrar.

• Assuming a mosque or "paper" talaq from abroad is enough.
  • Not sending a copy of the notice to the wife.
  • Forgetting dower and maintenance claims.
  • Remarrying before confirming divorce validity.
  • Using unqualified agents for forms.

faqs.question: Is a UK or US divorce valid in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: It can be recognised under Section 13 CPC if the foreign court had jurisdiction, followed due process and the decree is not obtained by fraud. For safety, also complete Bangladeshi formalities.

faqs.question: How long does talaq take in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Under Section 7 MFLO 1961, 90 days from the notice to the Chairman unless revoked, with a longer period if the wife is pregnant.

faqs.question: Can I divorce from abroad without going to Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes, through a notice served by post or an advocate and a Power of Attorney, though some Family Court stages may require attendance.

faqs.question: Does the wife still get dower after a foreign divorce?
faqs.answer: Yes. Unpaid dower remains a debt that can be claimed in the Family Court.

faqs.question: Who gets custody of children after divorce?
faqs.answer: The Family Court decides on the child's best interests; mothers commonly keep young children.
